← Walk-in tub bid calculator

How much to charge to install a walk-in tub

Bath remodelers get shopped on a published $3,499 walk-in tub installed Facebook special. Those numbers cannot see the alcove or the unit. An acrylic soaker into an existing alcove with an inward door is a different job from an extra-wide whirlpool with a drain relocate, a tile surround, a cast-iron demo, and a sistered floor.

Open the free walk-in tub bid calculator

Price the alcove and the unit, not the $3,499 dump

A walk-in tub is an alcove, then a unit, then a door. An alcove swap pulls the existing tub and sets the new one on the same drain. A relocate moves the drain or the supply. New construction has no demo. A custom opening widens the alcove or converts a shower. Matching an installed special on a relocate-plus-tile job is how a sold aging-in-place install becomes a loss when the plumbing and the surround eat the margin.

Soaker versus whirlpool on the same alcove

Homeowners usually start from the soaker special, then ask whether a whirlpool or an extra-wide unit is “a little more.” On the same alcove and the same door it is not a little more. A whirlpool is a pump and a GFCI. Extra-wide is handling and often a floor. The calculator prices all five units on the bath you already counted so you can quote the upgrade instead of matching the soaker number on a whirlpool job.

An alcove swap is not a drain relocate

The cheap special is almost always an acrylic soaker into an existing alcove, an inward door, no tile, no cast-iron haul. A relocate extra-wide tile job is a different crew day. Matching a published installed number on that job is how a sold aging-in-place install becomes a loss.

This is not a walk-in shower, a hot tub, or a toilet swap

A walk-in shower is tile, slope, and glass — a wet area, not a tub with a door. A hot tub is an outdoor spa with a crane and a pad. Toilet replacement is a commode swap. Water-heater replacement is a tank. This prices a walk-in tub: the alcove, the unit, the door, and the extras.

Walk-away price

Load the wage with payroll burden. Add overhead as a share of direct cost. Then take margin as a share of the customer’s price, not a markup on cost. The walk-away number is total cost. A proposed price under that number loses money before you take anything out of it.

They already bought the tub

Owners also shop a second special: “I already bought one on Amazon — just install it for $995.” Zeroing the tub invoice drops the bid. The set hours stay. A drain that does not line up or a missing overflow kit is a second trip. The $995 soaker special can cover if their unit fits; the $1,499 showroom whirlpool special still loses. See should I install a customer-supplied walk-in tub for both worked examples on the same bath.

They want Saturday after a fall

Families also call with a weekday number and ask you to start Saturday so she is not climbing the old tub. After-hours is time-and-a-half plus a second evening trip — you cannot leave the alcove open overnight. On the sample rates an acrylic soaker prices about $3,757.32 when they leave and $4,407.98 after hours. A $3,499 Saturday number covers the weekday and loses $27.39. A $5,800 Saturday whirlpool number loses even on the weekday. See should I take a Saturday walk-in tub call.

This page is a walkthrough of the arithmetic in the walk-in tub bid calculator. It is not a building-code determination, an accessibility approval, a plumbing design, or a price you should copy onto a contract.

Common questions

How much should I charge to install a walk-in tub?

Charge from tub count, unit, alcove, door, and extras — not a published $3,499 installed special. An acrylic soaker into an existing alcove with an inward door is a different job from an extra-wide whirlpool with a drain relocate, a tile surround, a cast-iron demo, and a sistered floor.

Is an alcove swap the same bid as a drain relocate?

No. An alcove swap pulls the existing tub and sets the new one on the same drain. A relocate moves the drain or the supply. New construction has no demo. A custom opening widens the alcove or converts a shower. Matching an installed special on a relocate-plus-tile job is how a sold aging-in-place install becomes a loss when the plumbing and the surround eat the margin.

How do the unit, the door, and extras change a walk-in tub price?

An acrylic soaker is the cheap-special unit. Cast is weight. Whirlpool is a pump and a GFCI. Air-jet is a blower. Extra-wide is handling. Inward swing is the cheap door. Outward is safer egress. Walk-through is a low threshold. Cast-iron demo, tile surround, grab bars, handheld, floor sistering, and a permit do not live in a published installed dump.

Is this the same as a walk-in shower, a hot tub, or a toilet swap?

No. A walk-in shower is tile, slope, and glass — a wet area, not a tub with a door. A hot tub is an outdoor spa with a crane and a pad. Toilet replacement is a commode swap. Water-heater replacement is a tank. This prices a walk-in tub: the alcove, the unit, the door, and the extras.

    Common questions

    Why is the tub itself half the price?

    Because that is what the job mostly is. On the defaults the unit and materials invoice at $1,875.60 against $643.19 of labor for 11.78 hours, in a $3,757.32 price. Walk-in tubs vary enormously in dealer cost — a soaker and a hydrotherapy unit with a heated seat are not the same purchase — so your invoice cost, not your hourly rate, is what decides whether this bid works.

    Is 11.78 hours realistic when installers quote two days?

    Those are usually two different scopes. This is the tub swap: demolition of the existing unit, setting and levelling, supply and drain connection, and the surround. The second day in a typical retail quote is normally tile or wall-panel finishing, an electrical circuit for the pump and heater, or a door widening — real work, but it is not in this number unless you add it.

    What is easy to miss when quoting one of these?

    Three things, in rough order of how often they blow up a job: the drain, because a walk-in tub needs a fast-drain path and an existing shallow trap arm may not give one; the electrical, since most powered units want a dedicated GFCI circuit; and getting the unit into the room at all — they are large, rigid, and frequently will not pass an existing bathroom door. Walk those three before you commit to a price.

    Should I be making medical or accessibility claims in the proposal?

    No, and this tool deliberately produces none. A walk-in tub is often bought for a mobility or safety reason, but grab-bar placement, entry height, and whether a specific unit suits a specific person are clinical and code questions, not pricing ones. Quote the installation; leave the suitability judgment to an occupational therapist or the applicable accessibility standard.

Should I install a customer-supplied walk-in tub?

Owners call with a box in the garage: “I already bought one on Amazon. Can you just install it for $995?” That sounds like free margin because the tub invoice left the bid. It did not leave the trip, the set hours, or the chance that the drain does not line up with their alcove.

Open the free walk-in tub bid calculator

Zeroing the tub is not a free install

A contractor-supplied acrylic soaker still carries the unit invoice. An owner-supplied tub that actually fits zeros that line and keeps the same set hours. On a typical cheap special — $42 wage, 30% burden, 15% overhead, 20% target margin, eight miles — the contractor-supplied bid is about $3,757. Zeroing a $1,850 soaker drops it to about $1,098, and the owner-supplied walk-away is about $878. Taking the Amazon special to “just install what they bought” at $995 keeps about $117 when the drain lines up. A drain that does not match still loses about $362.

Set hoursSameSameSame, plus an inspect trip
Walk-away on the cheap specialAbout $3,006About $878About $1,357
At $995 install-onlyLoses about $2,011Keeps about $117Loses about $362

The $1,499 showroom special is a different job

The $995 Amazon special is usually a cheap soaker. The job people actually buy is a whirlpool with grab bars: they paid $4,200 at a showroom and want you to “just set it for $1,499.” Same calculator, same owner-supplied rows. On the typical aging-in-place alcove — whirlpool, outward door, grab bars, handheld, permit, 14 miles — owner-supplied walk-away is $2,082.34. $1,499 still loses $583.34 even when the unit fits. A wrong drain walks away at $2,561.39.

So $995 can cover a soaker that fits, and $1,499 still loses on the whirlpool they actually bought. Load the typical aging-in-place preset and put their number in “price you’re considering.” None of those sentences is advice to take or refuse the crate.

Wrong drain is a second trip

Amazon listings skip the template. Drains come in on the wrong end, overflow kits are missing, and the door seal they expect you to eat is not in the box. Setting the wrong unit means a second dispatch plus hardware. Price that callback on the same alcove before you agree. The calculator adds a starting inspect trip and a missing-kit line on top of the rates you already typed.

How to use the comparison

Open the walk-in tub bid calculator, enter the bath you are standing in, and put their install-only number in “price you’re considering.” The who-supplies table scores that number against you-supply, owner-supplies-it-fits, and owner-supplies-wrong-drain. Nothing is uploaded.

This is the same arithmetic as how much to charge to install a walk-in tub. They want Saturday after a fall? See should I take a Saturday walk-in tub call. It is not a building-code determination, an accessibility approval, a plumbing design, or a reason to refuse a customer — it is the walk-away number on each supply path.

Common questions

Should I install a walk-in tub the customer bought on Amazon?

Only after you price the set without the tub invoice. Setting their unit is still a trip and crew hours. A $995 install-only special often covers that walk-away when the drain lines up, and loses money when the overflow kit is missing or the drain does not match.

Does a customer-supplied walk-in tub make the $995 installed special profitable?

Only if the unit actually fits. Zeroing a $1,850 soaker invoice drops the bid, but loaded labor, door hardware, travel, and overhead stay. On a typical alcove swap the owner-supplied walk-away is about $878, so $995 keeps a thin margin. A drain that does not line up or a missing overflow kit adds a second trip and walks away about $1,357.

What if they bought a showroom whirlpool and want $1,499 just-set?

That is a different job than the $995 soaker special. On a typical aging-in-place alcove — whirlpool, outward door, grab bars, handheld, permit — the owner-supplied walk-away is $2,082.34. $1,499 still loses $583.34 even when the unit fits. A wrong drain walks away at $2,561.39.

What if the Amazon tub does not fit the alcove?

That is a second dispatch plus a drain kit or overflow they did not have. Price that callback on the same bath before you agree to install whatever they rolled into the garage. The calculator adds a starting inspect trip and missing-kit dollars on top of your current rates.

Should I take a Saturday walk-in tub call?

Families call after a fall: “Can you start Saturday? Same $3,499 — she is not climbing that tub again.” That sounds like the same alcove. It is not the same crew day. After-hours is time-and-a-half. Open the free walk-in tub bid calculator

Saturday is not the weekday bid

A weekday soaker still carries the wage you already timed. After-hours raises that wage to time-and-a-half and adds a starting second trip. On a typical cheap special — $42 wage, 30% burden, 15% overhead, 20% target margin, eight miles, acrylic soaker, alcove swap, inward door — the weekday bid is $3,757.32. After-hours is $4,407.98. The walk-away jumps from $3,005.86 to $3,526.39. Taking $3,499 to “just do Saturday” covers the weekday and loses $27.39 after hours.

vs-a-flat-installed-special.html.text:
← Walk-In Tub Bid Calculator

This calculator vs. a flat "$3,499 installed" walk-in tub special

"$3,499 installed" is not a price for a walk-in tub — it is a price for one specific alcove, one tub, and one door, quietly applied to every bathroom the postcard goes to.

What a flat "$3,499 installed" special is

A flat installed rate is the fastest way to quote: one headline number on a postcard, a Facebook ad, or a website, next to a photo of a tidy bathroom. Homeowners shop it because it is easy to compare between bids, and it is the number an owner holding a competitor's flyer — or a family arranging an install after a fall — will ask you to match on their own bathroom.

The number behind it was set for one job — usually the cheapest configuration (an alcove swap on the existing drain, an acrylic soaker, an inward-swing door, no demo, no tile, no floor work) — and then reused for every tub afterward, whether or not the next bathroom looks anything like the one the rate was set on.

What this calculator is

This page keeps no account and sends nothing to a server. You enter the tub count, alcove scope (swap, relocate, new-construction, or custom-opening), tub (acrylic soaker, cast, whirlpool, air-jet, or extra-wide), and door (inward, outward, or walk-through), along with extras such as a cast-iron demo, a tile surround, grab bars, a handheld, sistering the floor, and a permit. It prices the scope, the tub, the door, and the extras separately, and returns a walk-away price and extra-work share below which the job loses money — for this bathroom, not a generic one.

Job$3,499 specialWalk-away priceVerdict
Cheap special: 1 acrylic soaker, alcove swap, inward door$3,499.00$3,005.86Covers, $493.14 to spare
Typical aging-in-place: 1 whirlpool, alcove swap, outward door, grab bars, handheld$3,499.00$6,912.34Short $3,413.34
Losing job: 1 extra-wide, drain relocate, tile surround, cast-iron demo, floor sister$3,499.00$11,522.08Short $8,023.08

Worked using this calculator's own starting kits at a $42 crew wage, 30% payroll burden, 15% overhead on direct cost, and a 20% target margin — the form's own defaults, not a number invented for this page. Open the calculator's presets to check any row yourself.

What a flat installed special doesWhat this calculator does instead
Charges the same installed rate whether the job is an acrylic soaker swapped into an existing alcove with an inward door or an extra-wide whirlpool with a drain relocate, a tile surround, and a cast-iron demo — several times the labor and material for the same "one walk-in tub." Prices the alcove from the entered scope, tub, and door, so the two jobs above come out at different numbers instead of one.
Prices "a walk-in tub" as one alcove-and-unit set, with no separate line for a drain or supply relocate, a whirlpool or air-jet pump and GFCI time, an outward or walk-through door, a cast-iron demo, a tile surround, sistering the floor, or a permit. Times the scope, the tub, the door, the demo, the tile, the floor, and the permit as their own extra-work hours, so that work shows up instead of being absorbed into the flat rate or skipped.
Assumes an alcove swap, an acrylic soaker, an inward door, and no demo, tile, floor, or permit, so a relocate, a whirlpool, an outward door, or a cast-iron demo gets quoted the same as a job that needs none of that. Adds relocate, tub-grade, door-grade, cast-iron demo, tile, grab bar, handheld, floor, and permit hours and material only for what was entered, so the two jobs price differently.
Bakes payroll burden into a round "installed rate" nobody re-derives, so the rate quietly drifts from the crew's real loaded cost. Loads the entered hourly wage by the entered payroll-burden percentage every time, so labor cost tracks the actual burden rather than a memorized rate.
Gives the installer a price to quote, not a number to check a quote against when a family asks to match a cheaper alcove-swap special on a relocate, whirlpool, tile-surround job — often on an after-a-fall deadline. Reports the walk-away price and the extra-work share of the job, so a shopped price can be scored against real cost before the installer commits to it.

A flat installed special is not wrong because it is simple — it is wrong when it is applied outside the one job it was built for, and nothing about a postcard rate tells you when that has happened. This calculator does not replace judgment about your market; it replaces the arithmetic a flat rate skips.

Common questions

Why does a flat "$3,499 installed" walk-in tub special get the price wrong?

Because the labor and material scale with the alcove scope, the tub, the door, and the extras, not with "a walk-in tub" alone. An acrylic soaker into an existing alcove with an inward door is a different job from a whirlpool with a drain relocate, a tile surround, a cast-iron demo, and a sistered floor. A flat installed rate quotes both the same and is wrong on one of them every time.

What does a flat installed rate usually leave out entirely?

The relocate, the pump, the tile, and the floor. A published installed price is set on the cheapest configuration it was ever quoted against — an alcove swap on the existing drain, an acrylic soaker, an inward door, no demo, no tile, no floor work — and has nowhere to put the hours for a drain or supply relocate, a whirlpool or air-jet unit's pump and GFCI time, an outward or walk-through door, a cast-iron demo, a tile surround, sistering the floor, or a permit. A contractor pricing off the flat rate alone is short before the alcove is opened up.

How much do the alcove, tub, door, and extras actually add over the flat rate?

On this calculator's own worked examples, at a $42 crew wage, 30% burden, 15% overhead, and a 20% target margin: the cheap special itself — an acrylic soaker, an alcove swap, an inward door — walks away at $3,005.86, comfortably under its own $3,499.00 flat rate. The typical aging-in-place job — a whirlpool, the same alcove swap, an outward door, grab bars, and a handheld — walks away at $6,912.34, $3,413.34 short of that same $3,499.00. An extra-wide tub with a drain relocate, a tile surround, a cast-iron demo, and a sistered floor walks away at $11,522.08 — $8,023.08 short, more than three times the flat rate on the same one-tub job. The scope, the tub, the door, and the extras move the number far more than "one walk-in tub" alone.

Is a flat installed rate ever the right way to quote a walk-in tub?

For something close to the one job it was actually priced on — an acrylic soaker into an existing alcove on the existing drain, an inward door, no demo, no tile, no floor work — a flat rate can land close, and on this calculator's own numbers that exact job comes in under it. The risk is applying the same number to a whirlpool or air-jet unit, a drain relocate, an outward or walk-through door, a cast-iron demo, a tile surround, or a floor sister without noticing, because the flat rate does not know which job it is looking at and neither does the installer until the alcove is opened up.

Does this calculator know what to charge in my market?

No. It has no data on local rates or what competitors charge. It takes the alcove scope, the tub, the door, and the extras, plus your loaded labor and overhead, and turns them into a walk-away price and extra-work share for the job you describe — the arithmetic a flat rate skips, not a market survey.

Nothing here says or implies that quoting a flat "$3,499 installed" special is a bad-faith practice — it is a common, honest shortcut that works until the job stops matching the one the rate was set on. This page describes where that shortcut breaks down, not a fault in anyone who uses it.

This calculator vs. Housecall Pro

Two different shapes: Housecall Pro is account-based field-service software for running a home-service business across clients, scheduling, and crews. This page is a free, private worksheet for one question — what should this walk-in tub install cost, given its alcove, unit, and access, before you quote it.

What each tool is for

Housecall Pro is a field-service management platform marketed to HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and other home-service companies. It is used to run CRM and customer records, scheduling and dispatch, online booking, invoicing and payments, and a mobile app for technicians in the field, tied to one account used on an ongoing basis across every job the company runs. Housecall Pro's own site is not reachable from this session to confirm today's exact plan names or dollar figures, so no price for it is invented here: only its well-documented identity and category — home-service field-service management software, sold as a subscription account — are stated, and no dollar amount for Housecall Pro appears on this page.

This calculator does none of what Housecall Pro does. It does not manage clients, schedule crews, send invoices, or collect payments, and it stores no customer or job record on a server. It takes alcove versus freestanding unit, door style, drain and valve rough-in, tile or surround repair, a customer-supplied unit, access, and the permit allowance, plus loaded wage, overhead, and target margin, and turns that into the walk-away price below which the job loses money and a copyable customer-facing bid summary — plus a printable customer proposal with scope lines and a signature block. It runs free in any browser, keeps no account, and uploads nothing you type.
